title: Tellers
description: Receive and pay out money. Keep records of money and negotiable instruments involved in a financial institution's various transactions.

tasks.text: Receive checks and cash for deposit, verify amounts, and check accuracy of deposit slips.
Monitor bank vaults to ensure cash balances are correct.
Cash checks and pay out money after verifying that signatures are correct, that written and numerical amounts agree, and that accounts have sufficient funds.
Count currency, coins, and checks received, by hand or using currency-counting machine, to prepare them for deposit or shipment to branch banks or the Federal Reserve Bank.
Examine checks for endorsements and to verify other information, such as dates, bank names, identification of the persons receiving payments, and the legality of the documents.
Prepare and verify cashier's checks.
Count, verify, and post armored car deposits.
Identify transaction mistakes when debits and credits do not balance.
Arrange monies received in cash boxes and coin dispensers according to denomination.
Receive mortgage, loan, or public utility bill payments, verifying payment dates and amounts due.
Process transactions, such as term deposits, retirement savings plan contributions, automated teller transactions, night deposits, and mail deposits.
Sort and file deposit slips and checks.
Perform clerical tasks, such as typing, filing, and microfilm photography.
Compose, type, and mail customer statements and other correspondence related to issues such as discrepancies and outstanding unpaid items.
Issue checks to bond owners in settlement of transactions.
Carry out special services for customers, such as ordering bank cards and checks.
Receive and count daily inventories of cash, drafts, and travelers' checks.
Order a supply of cash to meet daily needs.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Balance currency, coin, and checks in cash drawers at ends of shifts and calculate daily transactions, using computers, calculators, or adding machines.
Compute financial fees, interest, and service charges.
Enter customers' transactions into computers to record transactions and issue computer-generated receipts.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Resolve problems or discrepancies concerning customers' accounts.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Answer telephones and assist customers with their questions.
Explain, promote, or sell products or services, such as travelers' checks, savings bonds, money orders, and cashier's checks, using computerized information about customers to tailor recommendations.
Obtain and process information required for the provision of services, such as opening accounts, savings plans, and purchasing bonds.
Process and maintain records of customer loans.
Quote unit exchange rates, following daily international rate sheets or computer displays.
Inform customers about foreign currency regulations and compute transaction fees for currency exchanges.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, IBM Notes, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.
